newsitem.title: USA: Dallas-based software vendor plans Internet IPO.
newsitem.headline: Dallas-based software vendor plans Internet IPO.

text.p: Mrcdrom.com Inc, a new company that plans to sell computer software through an Internet catalogue, said it will go public with an initial stock offering directly to investors exclusively on the Internet.
The company said that it has filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission for permission to sell up to 3.0 million common shares at $4.00 each.
There will be no underwriters and investors may buy shares at a minimum subscription of 50 shares. Mrcdrom.com will have 7.5 million shares outstanding after the offering.
Net proceeds from the offering will be used for additional working capital, according to spokesman Kevin LeBlanc.
Mrcdrom.com was formed last month by Camelot Corp, a Dallas-based company that transmits telephone calls over the Internet. Camelot will retain a 60 percent stake in Mrcdrom after the offering.

Mrcdrom.com said it is currently test marketing at its World Wide Web site an Internet catalogue for products it will offer. The Web address, http://www.mrcdrom.com, is expected to become fully operational during the next few weeks, the company said.
